topic: Ox Alpha Review 2026: OpenRouter's Stealth Frontier Model

key_points: Ox Alpha is a stealth model on OpenRouter, released Aug 20, 2026, developed/operated by an anonymous third-party provider
1M (1,048,576) token context window; accepts text, images, and video as input, returns text
Positioned as a reasoning model for coding, sustained agentic work, and production workloads
Revealed to be ZAI GLM-5.3-Flash; prompts/completions retained by provider but not used for training
Reverse engineering via prompt injection and gzip-NCD compression analysis reveals Ox Alpha is GLM by Z.ai
Extracted system prompt: model must identify itself strictly as 'ox-alpha' from an undisclosed organization
Parametric memory tests and bi-directional factual probes showed weak/outdated training data — not Gemini-like
Distinct 'big model feel' that climbed the OpenRouter leaderboard
Behavioral fingerprinting: exact 11-of-11 tokenizer match to GLM-5.x vocabulary
Censorship is a 'switch, not a tilt' — bimodal profile; censors 7 topics (domestic incidents, Xi Jinping) while answering Xinjiang/Taiwan like American models
On Xi and domestic legitimacy topics, statistically indistinguishable from DeepSeek V4 Flash (most censored tested)
About a sixth of DeepSeek's overall censorship magnitude; concentrated in domestic political risk areas
A mysterious free AI model impressing developers; nobody knew who made it
Coverage of the identity-mystery angle and developer enthusiasm
Free model driving adoption and speculation about provenance
Z.ai confirmed Ox Alpha is a new GLM-series model and will release its weights
435 points on Hacker News — major industry confirmation
